designation: CLOSE ADDENDUM. Not a generation, and there is no generation 11. The closing ruling of 2026-08-26 ended the technical work; the operator ruling of 2026-08-28 section 2 authorised exactly one bounded refinement afterwards -- chart G's ten unrefined witness pairs, the barriers recounted over what survives, the register updated, chart L excluded by name -- because WIT-02, the operator's own rule enacted at close, had opened a coverage gap under the ridge, which the closing ruling had declared safe. It ran. The same ruling enacted DOC-08 and ordered one sweep of the claim surface against it. After this the technical work ends for good.
termination_condition: T-1 was reached at generation 6. G7-R, G8, G9 and G10 were bounded generations ordered post-termination; each opened no new scientific scope and each was followed by another, which is why this file records `closed` as well as `terminated`. The closing ruling forbids a further generation by name -- no G11, no S-5, no S-2, no fourth chart, no minimum-energy path -- and permits exactly one check, constrained to arithmetic over existing artefacts. That check ran, needed no solve, and is recorded under `free_check`. The addendum of 2026-08-28 does not reopen any of that: it opens no specification clause, adds no chart, no window and no witness, and brings one pre-existing rule into compliance on one pre-existing set. Its authorisation names its own scope and the run enforces it -- RefinementScope in scripts/run_wit02_chartG.py is hashed before the first solve and names one set.

schema.champion_commit: The last CONTENT commit, by definition. Never the commit that wrote this file: a state file cannot name its own commit, because its bytes are part of the tree that commit hashes. Guarded by tests/test_loop_state_close.py.
schema.bookkeeping_commit: null at write time, always. Nothing may fill this during the commit that writes the file, because the value would be that commit's own hash.
schema.machinery_commit: Equal to champion_commit. The addendum's measurement ran against the working tree that became that commit, byte for byte: the run executed, then the artefacts and the code that produced them were committed together. The distinction the earlier files draw between the tree a measurement ran against and the tree carrying its results does not arise, and each artefact additionally pins its inputs by SHA-256.
schema.baselines: REP-01 as amended at generation 9 section 3: every entry is an OBJECT carrying the invocation that produced it, never a bare scalar. Entries marked rerunnable are re-run and compared; entries that are not carry conditions and measured_at_commit instead.
schema.free_check: The one measurement the closing ruling section 5 permits. Recorded separately from `spec_clause_status` because it is a DESCRIPTION and not a clause: it was ordered after the data existed, so no pre-registration is possible and none is claimed.
schema.addendum: The one solving step authorised after the close. Recorded as a MEASUREMENT with a pre-registration, which is the opposite of what LOOP_STATE_v8.json had to say about its free check and for the same reason: the record must match what happened. addendum.question: does the chart-G ridge survive when the ten witness pairs that had never been refined are refined?

addendum.status: MEASUREMENT with a pre-registration. The scope, the battery, the recount rule and the outcome table were written to disk with their hashes before the first solve, and every later phase recomputes them and refuses to run on a mismatch. This is not the close's free check: that one solved nothing and was recorded as a description; this one solved.
addendum.new_solves_note: counted as I-V curves rather than as bias points: thirteen witness pairs and one null-control pair through six refinement rows each, plus the barrier paths for the full set and for the counted subset with their null controls. The artefacts are authoritative; this integer is an order-of-magnitude statement that the step solved, which is what distinguishes it from the close.
addendum.result: Twelve of the thirteen chart-G witness pairs stay below the distinguishability floor at every one of the six refinement rows. One -- pair 12, the pair with the least headroom at 98.9% of the floor -- rises through the floor at N=1201 and is withdrawn as a solver artefact. Recounted over the twelve survivors under generation 9's imported barrier criterion and generation 10's registered classifier, the set is still a RIDGE: six of twelve pairs at or below the floor barrier, 0.500 against a pre-registered ridge_fraction of one third. The median barrier is 0.808 floor units where the unrefined thirteen-pair set gave 1.039 -- a median 19.2 per cent BELOW the floor barrier where it had been 3.9 per cent above it. Every barrier is an upper bound, so the bound direction and the refinement push the same way.
addendum.why_it_did_not_flip: the pair that separated was one of the seven ABOVE the floor barrier, at a depth of 13.57 log-units, so the six pairs the classification rests on were untouched and the median fell through them. That the classification was never at risk from this particular pair is a measured outcome and not a reason the run was unnecessary: which pair would separate was not knowable before the battery ran, and the pre-registration says so.
addendum.reported_either_way: the outcome table was hashed to disk before the first solve, keyed on the classifier's own output, and the ruling pre-registered the reporting: a flip was to be stated in the same paragraph as the classification. A BASIN or MIXED outcome had a written home before the run started.

controls.D1_determinism: PASS. The pipeline was run twice -- once phase by phase, once in a single invocation -- and refine.json, recount.json and the register are identical apart from wall-clock fields.
controls.H1_inherited_hashes: PASS. The barrier criterion hash matches the one registered at generation 9 and at generation 10, and the ridge/basin decision hash matches generation 10's. The run raises rather than continuing on a mismatch.

addendum.free_finding: Generation 10's reading that survival is predicted by headroom against the floor reproduces on a second set, in a different chart at a different dimension: the twelve survivors are the twelve smallest distances at N=301, maximum 0.019543 or 97.7% of the floor, and the single pair that separates is the largest, 0.019779 or 98.9%. Perfectly ordered again. The location of the split moved, though -- chart J's sits between 92.2% and 93.65% of the floor and chart G's between 97.7% and 98.9% -- so the ORDERING transfers across two charts and two dimensions and the THRESHOLD does not. That is the arithmetic reason WIT-02 declined a margin band, now measured on two sets rather than argued from one. Reported either way; it is not what the run was authorised to establish.

open_findings.note: Narrowed once more at close, by arithmetic rather than by measurement. Generation 10 killed the localisation mechanism and left the question 'why is the leading direction fixed while the ones behind it cross the noise floor'. The free check answers the descriptive half: the leading direction is not merely fixed, it is FALLING -- by a factor of 1.195 and 1.148, spearman -1.000 and -0.983 -- which is the wrong direction to raise a count against an absolute cutoff, and the climb is carried entirely by the trailing values rising toward it. 95.6% to 97.9% of each trailing value's motion is in the normalised spectrum. So the phenomenon is the spectrum FLATTENING, and the open question is why widening the bias window compresses the sensitivity spectrum toward its own leading direction. Nothing here answers that and the ruling forbids chasing it. Untouched by the addendum, which measured no spectrum.
